gold_diagnosis: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with choroidal detachment

1: The patient has posterior scleral enhancement on MRI, which is a hallmark of posterior scleritis. The presence of vitreous cells, choroidal detachments, and retinal detachment also supports this diagnosis. The lack of response of the retinal detachment to corticosteroid treatment may indicate a more chronic or severe form of the disease.

The patient presents with painful vision loss, vitreous cells, and choroidal detachments, which are consistent with posterior scleritis. The presence of late leakage on fluorescein angiography and shallow subretinal fluid on optical coherence tomography also support this diagnosis. The improvement in choroidal detachments with corticosteroid treatment further suggests an inflammatory etiology.
